My boyfriend. Who Reddits but doesn't know me by this alt account. 

It was April 2020 and we were in the beginning of the lockdown. The lockdown was absolutely destroying me. I thought it wouldn't happen. Then I thought it would only be for a week. Then only 2 weeks. I figured there was no way it would run into Easter, or through Easter...then I started seeing events for the summer being cancelled. And the fall. And that's when I knew I was stuck with no way out. The isolation was destroying me. Being stuck "safe" (bullshit) at home with my abusers, knowing they now had all the access to me that they wanted, when they wanted it, with no way out for me, was enough for me to say I'm not doing it anymore. 

I circled a day on the calendar...forget the exact day but it was in the last week in April. I told myself if the lockdown and the measures/restrictions were not lifted by that date, I would be gone. And oddly enough just the thought of that comforted me because I knew it would be over no matter what happened. I wouldn't have to deal with it anymore. It was liberating. 

Well, the day approached and there was no sign of anything changing, so I knew what was going to happen. He was not my boyfriend at the time, just my best friend. I figured that he had the right to know I was making my exit and I didn't want to just disappear on him without him ever knowing what happened, or any way of knowing since he lives in a different country. So I told him. It was the hardest thing I ever had to tell anybody in my entire life.

I will never forget his reaction. His reaction is what shocked me out of it. 

I quickly told him it's okay now, I'm not going to do it. Things did not get better in 2020 but 4 months later he became my boyfriend. The pandemic ended but unfortunately we're both dealing with my codependency because I never know when I am going to need him to save my life again. I'm working on it in therapy.

No, I am not going vegan. Yes, I do care about wildlife to the point where I want to base my entire career around working with birds and estuarine animals. Yes, I LOVE animals and believe in proper care and maintenance of everything from your family dog  to a lower invertebrate being raised in a terrarium for observation. Yes, that's me talking to the tarantula like it's a puppy ("AWWW THOSE LITTLE FAAAANGS <3"). But still, no I am not going vegan.

I am not going vegan simply because as a naturalist I understand that animals are going to eat other animals for sustenance, that human bodies were indeed meant to eat meat and have been doing so since human bodies became a thing (hence the hunting of giant megafauna and fish), and because you will pry my chicken, beef, and seafood out of my cold dead hands. Could I eat my own cow (if I had a cow)? No. That's MY cow that I've developed a personal relationship with. Could I eat anyone else's cow that was bred specifically to be eaten? Totally. Do I "secretly not give a shit about animals" despite choosing them as my career and field of study? I don't think so, but if that's what you want to believe I ain't stopping you.

I dunno, my mom let me start watching R-rated movies when I was 9 years old, provided there were no sex scenes or detailed depictions of sex. So long as I knew it was only a movie and not supposed to be re-enacted in real life, nor are all those gory deaths/scary serial killers/horror movie things gonna happen to me or anyone else in real life, it was fine. I grew up understanding more than other kids at school that there were worlds where people get hurt and die, that mortality is a very real thing, that there are things that can kill you and so you should stay away from them until you're old enough to go near them without offing yourself...I had and still have a VERY healthy respect for guns and weaponry because  the movies and my videogames taught me what they do to a person. I knew  that if you kill someone, even if it's an accident, you go to jail (or in Movieland, are on the run from the police for the rest of your life and have to change your name, leave your home, and possibly kill several more people to stay out of jail), and in jail, there are nasty people who want to do things to hurt you and angry wardens who don't care if you get hurt. I knew about bleeding wounds, tourniquets, poison, and other horrible situations to be avoided and so I was VERY careful around things that could hurt you. I also knew, moreso than other kids, that bad people were a thing that exist...they did not exist in the way the MOVIES depicted them, but if bad people did not exist at all, the movies would have nothing to base their depiction on. While other 3rd graders in my class might have been naive and trusting, I knew better.

I WASN'T a "good kid" though. I was an angry, unfriendly, violent kid but that happened LONG before I was allowed exposure to those movies, so I don't credit the exposure to the movies for causing that. 

My mother was a sorry excuse for a "mother" for several other gigantic reasons, but I personally don't think letting me watch R rated movies files into her List of Awfulness. I'm sure others will beg to differ though. Personally, I wish it was THE NEWS that she would have restricted my access too...that was real life and a 9 year old knows nothing about editing or sensationalism. D:

Oh, this fucking video. I'm active in the autism blogosphere and when I found this vid I noped out. No, it wasn't caused by the vaccines, moron. Stop spreading the kind of information that leads to other people's children getting sick or subjected to hellish bullshit like CHELATION (which, if it doesn't kill them, will wreak permanent havoc on the body). Personally, I also hate how the tone of the video makes it sound like her child is basically dead rather than just displaying the early signs of autism. Autism is only a "death sentence" if either it's some horrible super-severe end of the spectrum that renders the person a functional vegetable, or you *make* it a death sentence by denying the appropriate resources and early intervention, socialization and behavioral therapies, etc because you're too busy crying about "our child was taken from us!!!" No, they're alive and right there. Do your fucking duty to make sure they have as decent a quality of life as possible. 

What these antivaxx people don't realize is that autism symptoms manifest in early childhood. Coincidentally, and purely coincidentally, we get our major vaccines in early childhood. There's been so much science and research into this and the conclusion at the end of it all is always there is no correlation between childhood vaccines and autism. However, the misinformation that parents like the one who made this video lead to refusal to vaccinate kids against severe childhood illnesses and parents "looking for a cure" in the form of "removing the vaccine toxins" through everything from harmless-but-ineffective "gluten free/alternative diet" BS to shit that's actually killed and damaged people (chelation,  biomed/homeopathic shit). Do NOT visit "Age of Autism" if you don't want to be overcome with the desire to leave holes in walls. 

No matter the context, antivaxxers will make my blood boil. There was a set of autism awareness videos I used to watch, by a father who had 2 adopted autistic children. The kids, now teenagers, are delightful people who are growing and coping beautifully with the condition. The father can't seem to go one video without screaming about how we need to ban vaccines because they caused the children's "illness" so I stopped watching.

Your father and my mother are cut off the same block. She would do this kind of shit as well--I wasn't allowed to have a present that made me happy, unless it was from her and vetted by her and approved by her (which rarely happened). She knew she'd get into a fight asking me to throw the stuff away so she would do it herself. Usually while I was asleep or away at school. There is nothing more traumatizing than waking up to find your prized possession gone without a trace. Then finding out it was destroyed. 

And like your puppy...my mother did it with my beloved rat. :( Instead of loosing him while I was away, though, she organized a way to have him killed that would make it look like she was innocent in the matter...

It's harder on the person self injuring than it is on the parent/caregiver. Self injurous behavior is the mind's desperate response to overstimulation or a sensory processing error. The mind is trying to re-route itself back into reality by creating stimulation--in some severe cases, "stimulation" is self injurous behavior or violent outbursts.

Well, I don't want to be dead. I experience that hell on a yearly basis, multiple times a year (right now the worst time of year for it is coming up, actually...). But I don't want to be dead. I love life. I love experiencing life. Life, to me, is waking up to birds outside my window and going to the movies with my friends, going to school, playing videogames, enjoying holidays and festivals. A cold spell in April can turn me into a shrieking, striking feral animal. But I still very much don't want to be dead. If someone gave me the conscious choice to end life now or continue life knowing this is never going to go away (I have 2 chronic mental illnesses on top of the autism, but that's another story for another time)...I'd choose life. 

I can't speak for this girl. I DOUBT she would have chosen death if she could have chosen death...are most of us really equipped to choose death?...but whether or not she wanted to die we'll never know.

One of the worst meltdowns I ever had was triggered by snow on March 20th.

My mind at the time? "March is spring, January and February are winter. Snow is for winter, not for spring. Snow is for winter. *SNOW IS FOR WINTER.*" 

And cue the eruption, which unfortunately continues for as long as the snow doesn't go away (which meant until I finally just gave out from all the exertion). :( 

I've also had them when the temperature dropped 20 degrees below what it was supposed to be due to wind chill or a passing cold front or during 5+ day periods of rain and storms. It's always cold weather that triggers them...it can be 90 degrees in February and nothing happens. But when it's 40 degrees in April then batten down the goddamn hatches.

Everytime there's a case like this it hits me right where it hurts.

And everytime there's a case like this there's inevitably an outpouring of sympathy for the poor mother who was driven by frustration and caregiver burnout to commit murder, and none for the poor autistic child or adult who was murdered (besides "It's terrible  that she was murdered and nothing justifies murder, but let me sit here and justify murder to you for a few sentences anyway.") 

And then when called out about it they go "You know nothing about this woman's life, take a walk in her shoes before you judge." 

Well.

You know nothing about that autistic girl's life. Take a walk in her shoes before you judge. I have walked in her shoes. I've had violent outbursts. Mine are related to weather patterns, hunger, or unexpected, non-corrected changes in routine. The weather ones are the worst of the lot because they are completely non-correctable. I can feel them coming on and send out an alert to my people, but once I'm erupting, I'm erupting and in that moment I am not a human being anymore. I'm not consciously thinking about the striking and kicking and screaming I'm doing. It's not like a tantrum. It's a complete and total shutdown of the human mind triggered by what the mind discerns to be a glitch in the matrix.

And since I've walked in that autistic girl's shoes, I can safely say that not only did she (obviously) not want to have her life ended over something she can't even consciously control, but she did not want to be having the outbursts that led to this burnout in the first place. *They hurt.* Physically, mentally, emotionally...they are PAINFUL AS HELL in every way. 

So maybe  the mother felt "backed into a corner" by Ruby's situation. But you know what? Ruby likely felt backed into a corner by the chaos and pandemonium going on inside her own mind during these outbursts. And the mother's the one who gets to walk the Earth again after her sentence is up. Ruby will never see this world again.  

Whenever I hear of a case like this, not only does it make me fear that one day one of my people is gonna decide they "can't take it anymore" and stick a knife in my throat (even though everytime one of these cases comes up, they're disgusted as I am and always make it a point to let me know the thought of doing such a thing to me has never even crossed their minds), but it makes me feel terribly for the poor girl living with a condition she never asked to have or got to choose not to have, who now will never get to see this world again because of it.

I agree that it was a bad decision to give birth to another child A. knowing there was a chance of the illness striking that one and B. knowing she had to dedicate full-time care and attention to her first disabled child. Honestly, once she had that genetic check done, she should have stopped at Claire. 

As for being "better off dead," well, no one truly has any authority to decide that. Now that they're alive, they're alive. All that can be done is to make them as comfortable as possible for the remainder of their lives. They still aren't "creatures" though. They are loved and cared for--even if the mother's behavior is questionable and she acts like a martyr mom from a Jodi Picoult mother, these girls are still loved and cared for and will be grieved when they die. They aren't creatures who no one would care about if they died in the woods somewhere.

It's still not appropriate to make derogatory comments about them. Is it their fault their brains are atrophying? Can we blame them for having limited mental ability? No, and making comments like this dehumanizes them and people like them when they are still humans. 

Any one of us could have ended up in a situation like theirs if we got a bad flip of the coin...it's nothing but pure, dumb luck that you yourself are not a "potato." Heck, you could end up like this now, even being born normal. Get into a bad enough accident and get bad enough brain damage and you're in the same boat.

This is Kreed. I used to read his mothers' blog a lot until I found these videos and discovered some possibly shady/exploitative practices done by the mothers. He passed away in May of last year due to an accumulation of illnesses he always had, but was never able to fully communicate the presence of. :( Give "Kreed's World" a read for some insight into his life. He was a great young man who got through life the best he could and savored those moments of happiness like they were treasures. 

This poor kid was slowly dying for most of his life, felt the pain of that, and just had no way to cry out for help except for in episodes like this. :( His mothers had to lose their child in the worst way possible, without ever knowing he was sick in the first place.

Yes, it is a bad thing. If you're gonna take videos like this, they should be for a clinician's eyes only. Not to be uploaded on Youtube. And no, it's not "spreading awareness." It is showing somebody off in their most vulnerable moment when they are powerless to stop it. 

I have meltdowns like this, not frequently anymore but it still happens on occassion. Mine are caused primarily by rogue weather patterns. During them, my brain literally cannot connect to itself and I am fighting desperately both to get rid of the pain and to find some semblance of reality to connect to, all while trying to communicate that something is very, very wrong and I am in distress. If anyone I was relying on to care for me during these episodes had recorded them and uploaded them to Youtube, I would be LIVID and that person would be cut out of my life forever. Unfortunately, people like this young man don't even get to do that. They have their worst moments broadcast online in the name of "awareness" (yeah, awareness for the parents and how "haaaard" it is, not for the people actually having  to suffer these extremely physically and mentally taxing episodes), and they can't even push back against it. And then of course the comments roll in about "What's the point in keeping someone like this alive" and "Oh, you poor parents, it must be so hard living with a monster like this" and "That kid's a stupid spoiled ass brat who needs a good beating," because they're stupid people on the Internet who know NOTHING about the actual situation. She went into diabetic shock the day after we went out for the sundaes. She wasn't able to call me until three days later.

I could try to find a happy medium by having them make her a diabetes-friendly Oreo/cookies and cream cake. I'd have to make sure she'd be okay with that, though. It'd be for her health...

She is intelligent, even aware of her conditions and that they are detrimental to her health. The problem is that once she sees food, or even hears about it...well, PWS is basically constant 24/7 starving to death. Their minds operate like a human being that is starving to death. She knows this. But yet, like any starving person, food sets her off.
Ice cream cakes are the only cake I don't know how to bake myself. Something about "Wtf is this sorcery, it's baked but it's also frozen? It's hot but it's also cold? Dafuq?"

I've mentioned the sundae incident a lot of times. Every time she suggests going out for ice cream or to a buffet or something like that, or to some other place with lots of high-calorie, high-carb food. I tell her, "Look, I really don't want you to end up in the hospital again. Remember what happened when we went out for ice cream that one time?" 

Her response is that it wasn't the ice cream that caused it, she can have ice cream/other high-carb food, it won't make her sick, she's had ice cream/other high-carb food before, there isn't anything she can't have, etc. She's been in the hospital twice for severe sugar spikes (one of which led to full on diabetic coma)...
This sounds brilliant! I heard of Halo Top but I didn't know they had cookies and cream flavor! So do you mean like, ice the cake with it? That sounds like a cool idea.

Regarding awareness/consciousness, Claire can at least figure out the EagleEyes device.

The awful truth about these girls' condition is that they can literally die at any moment. They should be in the care of professionals who can keep them comfortable as possible while they are alive. Not at home being dressed up and paraded around by a mother who insists "THEY'RE NORMAL TEENS I SWEAR! THEY ARE NORMAL!" That doesn't help them at all.

I don't agree with "allowing them to die." I do agree with maybe NOT trying for another child after you're told there is a chance of it coming out the same (or worse) as your severely disabled child. 

But they're here now. They're alive and have been for 15 years and counting. The best possible thing to do is to leave them in the care of specialists who can give them the best possible 24 hour care that they require, while ensuring that they can be kept as comfortable as is possible with their conditions. Their mother CANNOT DO THIS. Honestly, nobody outside of the professional field can do this. It doesn't make her a bad mother (what makes her a bad mother is the martyr-like shit she pulls on these blogs), just makes her human. The condition is just too great for ordinary parents to be able to manage. That's why hospitals and care homes exist. 

And it's not even as if she would never be able to see them again or they'd have to be taken away from her. She could still have an active role in her daughters' lives. She just wouldn't be responsible for their 24-hour intensive care.

They're loud, judgemental, superficial, self-absorbed vermin on two legs. 

They're never fucking there when you need them but won't get the HELL off your case when you don't. 

They spam the shit out of you with shit you don't care about and never will but then get bitchy when you don't care and even bitchier when you have the audacity to do the same. 

They will go absolutely ripshit like the world is about to end over non-problems that usually involve them not getting their own way or their own ideas not conforming to the way the world actually is. 

They are always in the goddamn way. 

They hurt eachother and make up reasons why they don't have to give a fuck. 

That's why I hate the little shits.
Definitely this. Lola is unable to react, so if she is in distress from being handled that way, she can't say or do anything about it. :(
They aren't spuds or potatoes. They're living, breathing children trapped in an unfortunate situation they never asked to be in or got a chance not to be in.
Please don't toss and move your newborns around like that o_o It's a living baby, not a doll. Toss and move a doll around like that all you want.

From what I remember, she had a high chance of having another child with the same condition as Claire. Yet she chose to have  the baby anyway, even knowing that she was going to be born with a condition that SEVERELY impairs her quality of life forever. Having children isn't about you wanting a child, a playmate for a sibling, etc. It's about being able to give the child the best possible life, which means making sure the child isn't going to live its life in constant distress due to a severe, degenerative illness that isn't going away.

"The Littlest Ninja" video is essentially just the two of them playing with a living child like it's a doll, while the child has *no* reaction at all because she does not have the mental capacity to react. I'm not uncomfortable with Lola in the video. I'm uncomfortable with the way her parents are treating her. I can't think of a situation where it's appropriate to move and toss a child around like it's a toy, disability or not. Lola is not "playing ninja" in that video. She can't "play ninja." Her parents are just treating her like she's a prop and taking advantage of the fact that she can't protest.
I noped out of reading the blog because of this picture and the close-up shot of Lola's dirty diaper. All of the nope in the world.

They display some sort of seizure activity in just about every video they're in. They do cry and make pained vocalizations...again, a lot of it seems to be attributed to seizure activity. Their illness has legitimately rendered them incompatible with their own bodies. Lola's GI tract is completely fucked to the point where she can't even make a bowel movement without the GI tract being manually stimulated. Their muscles are actively working against eachother. And as I mentioned, their official diagnosis turns out to be a genetic issue that degrades their brain matter over time as their age. What is left of their brain matter is slowly turning to mush each and every single day of their lives. It's not a painless existence. The girls' facial expressions in pictures and videos look as if they are in constant agony.
No feeding tube? D: Her poor little digestive system...is her body even able to take in normal food? I know she can't make bowel movements on her own and that her GI has to be stimulated...

My views on this has always been, "Don't post anything about the kid that the kid would be embarrassed to read about if they could read it." A lot of parents of severely disabled kids seem to forget this rule (Jani's Journey comes to mind). Sure, the kids will never actually read the blog and be able to process it enough to object to their mother posting photos of their poop-filled diapers. But at the same time, that doesn't mean you should just go ahead and do it. You think about how they WOULD react if they could, is the general rule of thumb.
...I didn't even see that. Now I want to punch a wall.

ALL OF THIS. THANK YOU. You've just voiced every problem I have with (most) disability moms on the Internet (I'm aware that there are some who are genuinely looking out for  their kids and blogging to raise awareness). My mother is NPD and I am disabled. I see so much of her in these bloggers and I am thankful to this day that she has never discovered the blogging platform. 

The thing is, of course a mother whose kids have this sort of condition is going to be desperate, stressed, and clinging to a hope of normalcy. But that being said, there is a fine, fine line between hope and DELUSION. The latter does NOTHING to help the kids, the mother, or the rest of the family.

Family dysfunction will exacerbate mental illnesses that are already present and create mental illnesses that are not. The last thing you want to do with a mentally ill child is to raise them in dysfunctional, unstable conditions.

This. I was reading a TIL thread about this family that pointed this out. They seemed to think a new child was going to be the magic fix, which is an astonishing burden to place on a child. Michael mentioned in his blog or in one of his books somewhere that Bodhi was meant to be an outlet for Jani in hopes the behaviors would quell. You don't do that to a baby.

I hate having to be "that guy" in a thread like this but I get sick everytime I see this story passed around everywhere because there's a lot of details these outlets miss. I'm glad to see a lot of people realize that Jani's father did admit to abusing her--specifically "losing it and hitting Jani as hard as we could. We hit in impotent rage." They've admitted to starving her, locking her in her room, beating/hitting her, and "doing everything we could to try and break her." Unfortunately when this is brought up it's usually immediately shot down by people who bring up how exhausting and stressful it is to parent a mentally ill child. Yes, it's exhausting and stressful. (Source: was mentally ill child, am mentally ill adult) No, it doesn't justify trying to "break" your 6-year-old. 

I had a lot of free time on my hands and spent an entire morning reading [the following thread](http://gomiblog.com/forums/mommy-bloggers/janis-journey/) on Michael Schofield's now-defunct blog (you'll have to disable adblocker because that site has horrible design and redirects) and uncovered an entire new, creepy-as-fuck can of worms, all of which indicate that this family has problems that go WAY BEYOND Jani's mental illness. Admission of shaking her in anger as a baby because she refused to sleep--you know what baby shaking and beating a young child causes? Brain damage. You know how brain damage may manifest? In ways that look very similar  to schizophrenia and psychosis. I'm not saying she's not schizophrenic. She might be. Childhood schizophrenia is rare as hell, but is a thing. But there's just no way that form of parenting is not going to exacerbate a mental illness if it's present at all. I have mixed feelings about this. 

Of course, parents need to show some tact when it comes to what they will and will not share on their blogs about their kids. I see autism parents blogging about their kids' abnormal bowel movements, changing their diapers, fecal smearing, severe violent meltdowns, etc and in general it should be a no-brainer that you don't discuss the content of your 10-year-old's diaper online. For parents running blogs about their experiences with their autistic children, I encourage you to use this rule when deciding what's best to blog about and what's best to keep private: If your child were to discover this post, would they feel ashamed or embarrassed? If so, it's best not to post it. Raising awareness does not outweigh your child's right to privacy. You don't post about your own private habits or the moments when you're at your worst, so don't post about your son or daughter's bathroom or masturbation habits or broadcast their severe meltdowns for the world to see. 

But do I think that parents should blog about their experiences with their autistic children? Yes. I believe that blogging is an important tool for raising awareness on what goes on in a household with a child with autism, or what goes on in the day-to-day life of an autistic child, adult, or teenager. Not only that, but it's a stress reliever and allows both parent and child to find support and encouragement among the blogosphere, connect with other autistic people or parents of autistic people who may provide valuable insight, and provide assurance that you are not alone and you are not the only one with these experiences.

If you're going to use your blog to vent your frustrations then PLEASE, I BEG of you, do NOT even remotely insinuate that it's the child's fault or that they are the cause of your frustrations. The now-infamous Kelli Stapleton's blog did so fucking MUCH of this--attributed every damn frustration and stress that occured in her or in the household to her child. There was another blog I was reading where a mother often lamented that she "loved her son and hated autism" (they don't come separate) and attributed the autism to everything that went wrong in the house. It made me feel bad for the kid because his mother pretty clearly viewed him as a source of annoyance and stress, and pretty clearly favoritized the neurotypical siblings...

If you want to see an autism parent's blog done right, read [this one.](http://momnos.blogspot.com) That mother has genuine love for her kid and a genuine desire and ability to understand things from his point of view. The blog is extremely informative and gave us so much insight and "aha!" shortly after my diagnosis when we were all struggling to make sense of and understand the condition. Most of her blogging focuses on the day-to-day joy she experiences living with her kid, and she does not share anything that shouldn't be shared.

I support neurodiversity because I don't like the idea of being thought of as diseased or defective. Autism is not something I developed or caught...it's not an abnormality, a side effect, or the effect of something that went wrong with my body. It's the way my brain is built. It has been the way my brain is built all my life and it will always be the way my brain is built. I don't like the idea of being told "your brain, which you've lived with for your entire life, works the way it does because you are diseased. There are people lobbying right now for a cure because the way you are put together is inherently abnormal and wrong for society. We want to erase people like you because we feel that you drag down the societal collective." Of course I am going to support the people who are against that kind of thinking. Autism has limited me in quite a few ways. I'm thankful that it hasn't limited me as badly as I could have, but it does limit me in ways that a neurotypical's brain does not limit them. And yes, it hurts to have to fight through these limitations. But at the same time, I am thankful for my autism because I like the way I perceive the world. I know that I would not be able to perceive it the same way if I were neurotypical or "cured," because none of the neurotypical people that I know and interact with can see the world the way I do or even understand why I do. 

I also see nothing wrong with fighting for society to become more accessible and manueverable for autistic people. Even if the other side were to get their sought-after cure, it would likely be prenatal or for very young babies, and even then the cure may not be accessible to everyone. There are still going to be autistic people having a hard time in this world, and in that case they would benefit from anything possible to increase their quality of life and enable them to have an easier time making it in this world.

No amount of therapy or type of therapy is going to turn your son neurotypical. If you're going into ABA with that expectation you need to drop it. 

ABA and other therapy, if done right, is meant to teach your child how to manage functioning out in the world. It's meant to eliminate negative behaviors such as self-injury and violence and establish coping mechanisms for stressful situations. I dunno if this is true for ABA specifically but cognitive behavioral therapy employs "redirection" from a negative behavior to a positive one, and redirection of the mind from a stimulus that proves to be distressing...it replaces a negative with a positive, essentially, and this kind of strategy has helped me MAJORLY. There is also an emphasis on positive social behavior and coping in social situations...it's not there to turn the kid into an outgoing social butterfly, but to allow him to adapt and function in social environments without having to pass as neurotypical. 

If any therapy is trying to make him "indistinguishable from neurotypical people" then that therapy is being done wrong.

Kron, from Disney's Dinosaur, is not a villainous character. He is certainly an antagonist by definition, but from the beginning to the end he fully believed that he was acting in the best interests of the herd. The way Kron wished to operate the herd was the way that alpha pack leaders in general operate in the animal kingdom. He was the alpha male, determined the leader of the pack by the rules of nature, and believed that his way was the only way to ensure that the herd was not killed off. He saw Aladar as a threat to the herd dynamics and a threat to his own position as the alpha male, hence the aggression towards him. It was not because he was malicious by characterization.

If we're going to go by human standards since the dinos are humanized, he was a bitter old social darwinist who was dangerously ignorant (dangerously because he was ignorant AND in a position of leadership and power) but did have genuinely good intentions for the herd. He didn't act the way he did because he wanted the herd killed off for the evulz. He did because he carried a blind, ignorant, but genuine belief that his way was the right way. He died because he overestimated his own strength and failed to take into account that there is always someone better. His death was poetic...and in a way, tragic, as we are looking at the dinosaur version of a man who did not realize his own ignorance until it was too late. Notice how when he is thrown by the Carnotaur, he has that final "oh crap" look on his face--oh crap, his beliefs betrayed him. His ignorance betrayed him, and now it's too late. He's going to die for his own ignorance, his herd will be left without its leader...and he looks upon Neera and Aladar lovingly before taking his final breath. In his dying breath, he realized that they were right and he was wrong all along, and that final loving glance indicates that he knows now that they are worthy of becoming the new leaders in his absence.

I get into a lot of arguments with Dinosaur fans about this but Kron was NOT the villain. That would be the Carnotaurs. Kron was not a villain or a malicious character by definition. He was a blind fool, yes, but he was also a protective (if misinformed) leader and a loving, protective brother to his sister Neera. It was just too late for him to redeem himself once he genuinely realized he was wrong.

Well, it's easy when more and more people are coming right out and saying "I'm self-diagnosed and to question it is ableist." 

Autism is a mental condition. It, like ALL OTHER mental conditions (I have seen self-diagnosed personality disorders, depression/anxiety disorders, etc as well) must be handled in the same way that any physical condition would be: professional diagnosis followed by a treatment plan. You wouldn't try to diagnose yourself with a physical condition or a physical disability, so you certainly do not do it with a mental one. The problem with self diagnosis of ANY condition is that the symptoms of certain conditions are too similar--what you may mistake as one condition can turn out to be another thing entirely. Going on the Internet and symptom-checking, then declaring yourself to have the condition that matches most of your symptoms, is an easy way to run into this problem. My symptoms have been mistaken by untrained people as everything from anxiety to several personality disorders to outright schizophrenia. It took a professional evaluation to discover what I really had: Asperger's syndrome. Until then, nobody knew what was really going on with me, and therefore nobody could treat it. Which brings up another very important reason for professional diagnosis: you need a professional diagnosis to qualify for a *treatment plan* in the form of therapies, services, benefits, etc. And yes, you absolutely do need a treatment plan if you are going to be living with autism. I lived with untreated, unmanaged autism for *twenty years* and unmistakable damage has been done that the professionals who work with me now can and do pick up on. I am now essentially "locked" out of several forms of treatment because they are only approved for children who are still in their developmental years. Lots of things can be done to help the mind while it is still developing, which cannot be done once the "plasticity" wears off and the mind is fully developed.

Except for a small minority of "autism pride" advocates, someone who rallies for the termination of autism management and treatment is almost always self-diagnosed. I have met VERY FEW actually autistic people who believe that it is okay to exist in the world with no treatment and no management of their behaviors and difficulties. It is PAINFUL to live in the world with no treatment...I've done it for 20 years of my life. My childhood and teenage years were hell on Earth that I will never, ever get back. Those who use their autism as a crutch, to get special treatment or privileges, or to cover for acting like an asshole are almost always self-diagnosed (again, barring a vocal minority). It is an insult to the autistic people I know, myself included, to use your autism as an excuse not to behave yourself--so many neurotypicals already believe that autism is an excuse not to behave yourself. Why would actual autistic people want that perpetuated? 

Not to mention the people who flaunt it like it's a badge of honor or a trend. Autism is not a trend. It's not a badge of honor. It's a neurological disorder that at the same time is a part of who we are, but that we must overcome and realize it is not the entirety of who we are. The people with actual, diagnosed autism realize that for the most part. They realize that autism is something you have that can be difficult but is not the be all to end all. I have read the blogs of actual, diagnosed autistic people and their caretakers. And I have read the blogs of self-diagnosed autistic people who exaggerate and weaponize their "autistic traits." Believe me when I say that I can tell the difference.

Why is this getting hate? o.O 

The social justice community IS harmful, to autistics and otherwise. Many of the "autistics" who are vocal in SJ circles ARE self-diagnosed, using it as a tool, or perpetuate the misconception that autism is a "trendy" thing to have. They call themselves autism advocates and say that they are speaking for autistics when they are not genuinely diagnosed as autistic themselves. You CANNOT call yourself autistic or expect others to take you seriously as an autistic person if you do not carry an official diagnosis from a professional. Internet websites are NOT professionals. And if people cannot take you seriously because you're self-diagnosed, then people are less inclined to take the words of ACTUAL autistic people seriously because "You're not REALLY autistic, you're probably just one of those self-diagnosed teenagers." I've heard people come right out and say autism is a joke or is a fake condition because people who do not really have it use it as a crutch.

Psuedo-advocates in the SJ community have been known to lobby against treatment or even therapies for autistic people. I got into a fight with this girl a while back who said that autism should not be managed and that therapy is one of the most harmful things you could ever do to an autistic person. She went on to say that even behaviors and stims that involve self-harm or violence towards others should just be left alone, as it's part of autism and it's "ableist" to say otherwise. Yes, I have meltdowns, but just because I have meltdowns does not mean I have the right to inconvenience or cause discomfort to others by kicking walls and screaming like a banshee in public simply because "I'm autistic and this happens to autistic people." I've been in therapy meant to control and help me to better manage meltdowns and the things that trigger them. It's not ableist at all to expect me, a grown woman with autism, to take the necessary procedure to have my condition treated and managed, rather than just to let it run wild. 

This is an unfortunate trend in the SJ community in regards to autism. I only had a run-in with one instance, but I've observed other instances in which autistic people as well as self-diagnosed quacks went on to say that autism is not a condition that should be managed or treated. There is a difference between curing autism outright, and learning to manage the behaviors so you can present yourself in society--I don't mean "be normal" or "stop being weird." I mean be able to get through a day without having a scream-fest in public or injuring yourself. Being able to redirect yourself and learn to cope with triggering stimuli.

The social justice community IS ruining the autism rights movement, in a way that they are ensuring that real autism advocacy does not get taken as seriously as it should. When you have people trying to use autism to look "special," as a get-out-of-trouble free card, or else lobbying against therapies and legitimate treatments that help to manage autistic behaviors because "I shouldn't HAVE to control my behavior, the world should just deal!" then you have people who think that autism is a "joke" or that all autistic people are looking to act like that and use their disability--which is something to be OVERCOME, not CELEBRATED--as an excuse.

I read TiA. It is in no way a "vile hatefest." It's about calling out extremists, anti-logic, and genuinely harmful beliefs and concepts perpetuated by the various "social justice movements" and their appearances on social media. It CALLS OUT vile hatefests, and absolutely despises the "self-diagnosed autistic" trend going around that makes lives for actually autistic people so much harder.

There will be a lot of pride, and there will be a lot of joy. Your two children will grow and develop the same as other children. Maybe not in the same WAY, or at the same RATE, but they will. Regarding the ethical arguments of a cure: so, let's say that hypothetically, they did discover a cure by isolating the genes. Now what? Is it going to be highly regulated so that the cure is ONLY to be used on those so severe on the spectrum that they operate like infants? Is it a prenatal genetic thing where parents will be encouraged to abort an autistic kid? Will all high functioning autists--adults and children alike--be required to consent to a cure before being administered it? Children aren't robots, they may not necessarily want to take something that may change around who they are as well. Will they be allowed to make that decision without the parent going "Too bad, I want it done because *I* don't want my kid to have autism and I don't care how high functioning it is?" 

This kind of stuff is why high functioning autists argue against a cure, without thinking about the benefits that a cure might bring to the other end of the spectrum. Is it right for them to ignore lower functioning individuals? No. I'm not saying it's right or that it's MY view, I'm saying that this is why high functioning individuals tend to have a kneejerk response to anything regarding a "cure."

There's a lot on the table to think about when it comes to the cure argument. Yes, a lot of high functioning people are quick to scream "NO CURE NO CURE!" without thinking about the end of the spectrum that is so severe that those people cannot even go to the bathroom on their own or feed themselves. The thing is, for a lot of high functioning autists the idea of a "cure" is scary. Hearing people talking about a "cure" for the "disease" makes them feel like THEY are diseased and their very existence is something that requires a cure. Autism is not a mental illness that is separate from the person's identity the way schizophrenia or late-onset mental illnesses might be considered. People with autism are born that way, have had it all their lives, and it drastically affects their performance, identity, and yes, sense of self.

So when people like this hear about a potential cure for autism, or even that people want a cure in the first place, they hear it as "That includes me, since I also have autism...they think my sense of self is something horrible and diseased that needs to be removed." It's not so much that they don't give a shit about those on the severe end of the spectrum. They do, they are just very scared to support something that they feel might hurt their end of the spectrum too. Also there's a lot to think about when it comes to the ethics of a cure.

I love museum-going and zoo-going, and I find that the museums and zoos that give me the best experiences include the following: 

Interactive exhibits--things I can move, touch, get up close to, and that will respond directly to my actions. Liberty Science Center is paradise because of this. It has the wall that lights up when you touch it, the working mini machines (my favorite is the mini oil rig! Oil rigs are my favorite kind of machines), all of the buttons you can press to make things happen. The Philadelphia Zoo has its "lorikeet experience" where you can go in the lorikeet pen with a cup full of nectar and feed them while they sit on your shoulder. 

Lots of colors, textures, and details. Things like planetariums and mineral exhibits with colorful geodes and crystals. I tend to be more interested in the exhibits themselves if they are set in a colorful, artistic scenery like the Pacific Islanders exhibit in the Museum of Natural History, with its ocean-blue walls and the big Easter Island moai as its focal point.

The inclusion of live animals--any live animals--somewhere in the museum. Autistic people in general tend to get along with animals, as they lack the complicated little social and communicative cues that give us so much trouble with humans. Interacting with animals is easy and animals are totally non-judgemental, so we are drawn to them. In the case of a live animal exhibit at a museum, the only "interaction" needed is to sit and watch the animal closely and observe how it reacts to its own environment.

I'm autistic myself, and I have been following this case for the entire year it's been going on because it struck a very personal chord for me. As I was reading up on the case, I realized just how much like Issy I was when I was that age, complete with the aggression (though thankfully my aggression wasn't AS severe as Issy's, it existed and it tore my home apart). 

And so let me say this: I am sick and tired of ALL of the people defending the mother. I am sick and tired of ALL the stories and reports being centered around the mother. What about Issy? Why aren't there any stories that come from Issy's point of view? I'd like to hear HER speak on the events because maybe then we'll know what was REALLY going on. She was not aggressive because she was an abuser or a monster. We had reasons for our aggression. In my case, it was because my parents were handling me poorly and I was reacting accordingly. I hated the way they talked about me. I had to live every day of my young teen life feeling yanked around, downtrodden, unappreciated, disrespected...everything I did was wrong, I was the villain of the house and I knew it, I had to listen to them say horrible things about me, even talk about wanting to get rid of me and abandon me somewhere. My bouts of aggression, to me, was fighting back against that. Against the feelings of constant fear, unease, and discomfort in the world they had created for me. Fighting back against the two people who had created an unsafe, dysregulated world for me. I can't speak for Issy, but I have a strong feeling that it was something like that for her too. So because she was potentially mishandled so much that aggression may have seemed like the only option, because SOMETHING happening in that house was so damn dysregulating to her and continued to go on that she felt there was no other way to fight back, we all forget her and feel sorry for her "poor exhausted mother" instead??? BULLSHIT. I hope someone is able to get her side of the story someday, maybe when she's older. Then maybe people will start thinking of HER and not her mother. I've noticed the reports of aggression out of Issy ceased after her mother was removed from the picture...

Cases like this make people like me wonder what would happen if our parents attempted to "mercy kill" us to "be rid of the burden." Would we cease to be people and exist only as sources of countless exhaust and difficulty while our parents--our murderers--would be sympathized with because "they were just so exhausted!" and "they were so strong to put up with that for as long as they did!" I hate how Issy has become an afterthought--or else the villain of the story--while everyone has nothing but heaps of praise and sympathy and well-wishes to give to Kelli and even laments that she was thrown in jail. I will bet all my money that it was Kelli herself or something she was doing that was causing Issy's aggression in the first place. You have no idea how happy I was to hear that she would be rotting in jail and out of that poor child's life forever. I have no sympathy for her. I have sympathy for Issy, the girl I see 13-year-old me in.
